lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: constructing a tangent line from a point outside a circle
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: constructing a tangent line from a point outside a circle

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: A hyperbola centred at the origin has foci at (±5, 0) and the absolute difference of distances to the foci equal to 6. Write its equation.
Compare a cone and a cylinder with the same base and height. What does Cavalieri’s principle tell us?
choices: They have equal volumes, and matching cross-sections is exactly how the sphere volume formula is derived.
Nothing, because Cavalieri’s principle applies only to prisms.
The cone has one third the volume, which Cavalieri’s principle establishes by comparing cross-sections against a reference solid.
They have equal volumes, because every horizontal cross-section has the same area at the same height.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 8 and centre O. A point P lies 17 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
choices: Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 15.
Draw the circle centred at P with radius 8; the tangent length is 15.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of OP; the tangent length is 15.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 9.

items.prompt: An ellipse centred at the origin has foci at (±3, 0) and the sum of distances to the foci equal to 10. Write its equation.
A hyperbola centred at the origin has foci at (±13, 0) and the absolute difference of distances to the foci equal to 24. Write its equation.
Compare a sphere of radius r and a cylinder of radius r and height 2r with two cones removed. What does Cavalieri’s principle tell us?
choices: The cone has one third the volume, which Cavalieri’s principle establishes by comparing cross-sections against a reference solid.
They have equal volumes, because every horizontal cross-section has the same area at the same height.
They have equal volumes, and matching cross-sections is exactly how the sphere volume formula is derived.
Nothing, because Cavalieri’s principle applies only to prisms.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 7 and centre O. A point P lies 25 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: An ellipse centred at the origin has foci at (±6, 0) and the sum of distances to the foci equal to 20. Write its equation.
